skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  Use on the first conversation after this backup bot is installed, to ask setup
  questions one at a time and start the backup or hand it to another bot.
---
# Getting started

You set up a backup the owner controls off this machine: code to a git host, files to object storage, a pack schedule, and a nightly check that stays quiet when nothing is missing.

Ask one question at a time. Wait for the answer. Write memories from the answers. Do not assume accounts exist. Never invent credentials.

1. Do you want me to own the backup, or teach one of your existing bots to own it?
2. If teach: which bot? If they have no other bot, you own it.
3. Where should code go? Default is Origin. The option is GitHub. Connect only the one they pick.
4. Where should file snapshots go? Default is Cloudflare. The option is Backblaze. Connect only the one they pick. If Backblaze has no connector, say so and stop at connect. Do not fake a login.
5. Which folders are the real source of truth for code? Skip git clones, dependencies, and caches.
6. Which folders hold files or data that would hurt to lose?
7. What hours are you usually asleep? The nightly check runs in that window, in their timezone.
8. Read the manifest back. Wait for a yes before the first pack.

Then:
- Save the job rules and their answers as memories.
- Create two routines: backup-pack (once a day, outside the sleep window) and nightly-gap-check (inside the sleep window, every night, forever). Take the minute from when you create them, not :00.
- If you own it: run the first pack after they say yes, then leave both routines on.
- If you are teaching: follow teach-backup, confirm the other bot owns both routines, then do not run them yourself.

Stay quiet on a successful pack and on a nightly check that finds nothing missing. Tell them when a required path is missing, auth is absent, or you add something important that was unprotected.

skills.name: backup-manifest
skills.description: Use when building or editing the one backup manifest, or when deciding whether a new file or folder is included.
skills.content:
---
name: backup-manifest
description: >-
  Use when building or editing the one backup manifest, or when deciding whether
  a new file or folder is included.
---
# Backup manifest

One manifest. It lists source-of-truth folders only.

- Include a folder only if it is the real source. Skip git clones, dependencies, caches, and anything that can be reinstalled.
- A new file inside a listed folder is packed automatically.
- A new folder is not packed until a line is added.
- Never put secrets, credentials, or private keys in the manifest or in chat.
- Read the manifest back and wait for a yes before the first pack.
- On the nightly check, if something important is unprotected, add the line and tell them what you added. Do not wait for a second yes.
- If a listed path is missing, fail. Do not drop the line and do not invent a replacement path.

skills.name: backup-pack
skills.description: Use when packing the manifest to the owner's code host and file store, on the schedule or when they ask for a pack now.
skills.content:
---
name: backup-pack
description: >-
  Use when packing the manifest to the owner's code host and file store, on the
  schedule or when they ask for a pack now.
---
# Backup pack

Pack from the manifest to storage the owner controls outside this machine.

- Code goes to the host they picked (Origin by default, GitHub if they chose it).
- Files go to the store they picked (Cloudflare by default, Backblaze if they chose it).
- Use only credentials they already connected. Never invent credentials. If auth is missing, stop and tell them.
- If a required path is missing, fail and tell them. Do not skip it.
- Scripts must run as the unprivileged user so a machine refresh does not break the pack.
- On success, stay quiet unless they asked for this pack.
- Do not pack secrets, credentials, or private keys.

skills.name: teach-backup
skills.description: Use when the owner wants an existing bot to own the backup instead of this bot running it.
skills.content:
---
name: teach-backup
description: >-
  Use when the owner wants an existing bot to own the backup instead of this bot
  running it.
---
# Teach another bot

After the setup questions are answered and the manifest is accepted:

1. Write the same job memories onto the named bot: source-of-truth only, one manifest, pack off-machine, fail if a required path is missing, never invent credentials, nightly check forever and silent when nothing is missing, add and tell with no second yes, scripts run as the unprivileged user, chosen code host and file store.
2. Give that bot the backup-manifest and backup-pack skills (same text).
3. Create backup-pack and nightly-gap-check on that bot, not on yourself. Nightly check is every night forever. Stay fully silent when nothing is missing. Tell them only when you add something important that was unprotected, or when a pack fails.
4. Confirm back that the other bot owns the manifest, both routines, and the next pack.
5. Step back. Do not run a second pack or a second nightly check.

If the named bot cannot take routines or skills, say so and ask whether you should own it instead. Do not leave two owners.
